newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Normandy sees second half improvement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Normandy sees second half improvement.

text.p: Normandy Mining Ltd said it expected results in the second half of 1996/97 to show improvements in all business sectors due to new operations, acquisition and an improved zinc price.

Colin Jackson, general manager, corporate affairs, told a briefing on Thursday night the company expected gold results to be similar in the second half to the first half pre-tax contribution of A$176.4 million plus an initial input from the Vera Nancy joint venture in Queensland.
The contribution from the Goldfields power project would be higher than the A$3.4 million achieved in the first half after only three months of operations, he said.

"Commercial minerals should be slightly higher (than the first half A$15.6 million) benefiting from the Australian Betonite acqusition and metals (A$24.8 million) higher due to an improved zinc price," he told the Day Cutten briefing.
Jackson said zinc had averaged US$0.40 cents per pound in the first half, while its current price was US$0.55 cents.
"Pre-tax profit improves by A$2 million per annum for every one cent per pound increase in the zinc price," he said.

Jackson said its La Source joint venture with the French-owned Le Bureau de Recherches Geologiques et Minieres (BRGM) on Monday had lodged an appeal in Peru in the latest round of its legal dispute over the Yanacocha gold mine.

The other stakeholders at Yanacocha, Peruvian owned Compania de Minera Beunaventura SA and Newmont Mining Co are seeking to exercise pre-emptive rights to buy a 24.7 percent stake in South America's largest and most profitable gold mine.
They launched legal action to prevent BRGM from transferring its stake to La Source.
Jackson said that under the framework agreement setting up La Source, the joint venture would receive 788 million French francs in compensation if it eventually lost rights over the mine.
